quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pick one spot in the lane and stay there at all times.
Move around the lane constantly to keep other drivers away.
Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where you position yourself in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on what is happening on the road and in traffic.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can cause the rider to enter another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Usually keeps the rider in their lane.
Is okay because motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause the rider to enter another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before you start a turn or curve.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Skip multiple gears at once.
Shift down one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way to neutral first.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Shift down one gear at a time. Release the clutch slowly through the friction zone between each downshift.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you:

options.text: When stopping will take longer than normal.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver ahead from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will take longer than normal.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. This includes slippery pavement, heavy traffic, or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: The proper body position on a motorcycle:

options.text: Sits you forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
Sits you as far back as possible and you have to stretch to reach the grips.
Leans you far over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keeps your knees far away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sits you forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips. This lets you reach and use the controls easily and comfortably.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after one drink before riding:

options.text: Guarantees you will not be arrested for drunk riding.
Guarantees your riding skills will not be affected.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not fully remove alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not fully remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: On average, the body removes about one drink per hour. The time needed varies, so the safest choice is not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a drink limit beforehand so you can still ride safely.
Not ride.
Not worry about your riding if you feel okay.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid the danger of riding under the influence is to not ride after drinking. Any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to ride.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid hitting an object or uneven surface, you should:

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Stand slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stand slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, approach it as straight as possible. Slow down as much as you can, keep the motorcycle upright, and stand slightly off the seat so your legs can take some of the impact. Just before contact, gently twist the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Are not important.
Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you cannot do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine. Also check them before changing lanes, at traffic lights, and before slowing down.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Ride more slowly than usual.
Start slowing later than usual.
Try to fit into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: The passenger's weight affects how your motorcycle handles. It will speed up slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride more slowly, start slowing sooner when stopping, leave more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for larger gaps before crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride if they have been drinking. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help talk them out of riding.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see you on your motorcycle?

options.text: Ride with your headlight off.
Wear bright clothing.
Follow other vehicles very closely.
Do not use turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright clothes. Also keep your headlight on at all times and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Assume they have ridden on a motorcycle before.
Do not assume they have ridden before. Explain what they need to do.
Do not answer their questions.
Do not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume they have ridden before. Explain what they need to do.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to know how to stay safe. Never assume they know what to do. Give your passenger clear instructions before every ride.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Safe if used correctly.
Safe even if used incorrectly.
Only for use if the rear brake fails.
Not meant to be used often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe if used correctly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used properly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides most of your stopping power.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for your motorcycle?

options.text: The one that lets you go fastest.
The one that lets you draft behind other vehicles.
The one where other drivers can see you.
The one in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one where other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where you can see others and they can see you. Avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should prevent other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What should you do for motorcycle safety?

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle works fine.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle is more serious than on a car. Always check your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce crash injuries?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose strong, durable materials for protection.

questions.question: Which surface gives the best grip for a motorcycle?

options.text: A gravel road
Dry pavement
Mud
Lane markings

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are all hazardous. Dry pavement is the safest.

questions.question: What does smooth downshifting do on a motorcycle?

options.text: It is not useful.
It lets the engine help slow you down.
It is illegal.
You should not do it around other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets the engine help slow you down.
questions.explanation: Downshifting can help slow your motorcycle using the engine. If you use engine braking, activate your brake lights so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?

options.text: Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest
On the left handle grip
On the right handle grip

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: What is the best source of information about your motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual
A book about motorcycles
A former owner
Someone knowledgeable about motorcycles

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual as your main source of information about your motorcycle. It tells you how to operate it, what it can do, and how to maintain it.

questions.question: When does alcohol impairment begin?

options.text: With the first drink
At about half the legal limit
At the legal limit
Only after multiple drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: With the first drink
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be impaired below the legal limit. Do not drink any alcohol before riding.

questions.question: What should you NOT check on your tires before riding?

options.text: Air pressure
General wear
Tread depth
Shininess

questions.correctAnswerText: Shininess
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear. Shininess is not important.

questions.question: Which surface is NOT slippery?

options.text: A dirt or gravel road
A strip of oil in the center of a lane
Mud on pavement
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. These include wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, oil, and metal plates. Dry pavement is not slippery.
